newsitem.title: USA: PP&L rates upheld by Commonwealth court.
newsitem.headline: PP&L rates upheld by Commonwealth court.

text.p: The Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court has upheld Pennsylvania Power & Light Co rates set by two state Public Utility Commission actions and remanded a third issue to the commission for recalculation, the utility said Friday.

In an opinion issued Tuesday, the court ruled the commission acted properly in allowing the PP&L Resources Inc subsidiary recover costs associated with post-retirement benefits for employees and deferred costs that dated back to the start of commercial operation for the Susquehanna Unit 2 nuclear facility.
On a third issue, the court ordered reconsideration of the collection of the state gross receipts tax on bills that go unpaid by electricity consumers.
The state Office of Consumer Advocate had appealed the commission actions following the commission's decision on PP&L's 1995 rate case, the company said.

The court decision will have no immediate effect on the bills of PP&L customers, according to Paul Russell, PP&L's associate general counsel. "The decisions on retirement expenses and on the Susquehanna Unit 2 costs simply confirm the commission's decisions on rates that are in effect today.
"On the gross receipts tax issue, we will await further PUC direction before taking any action," said Russell.
The post-retirement expenses, which were related to changes in financial accounting rules, are being collected over 17 years at an annual rate of about $1.7 million.

The Susquehanna Unit 2 costs, which were incurred between the commercial operation date of the facility and recognition of the unit in company rates, are being collected over a 10-year period at an annual rate of about $1.9 million.
The gross receipts tax issue amounts to about $740,000 per year, the company said.
